connector: Imagine a dinner where your seat shows everyone how important you are. That was a royal court. Today’s article explains its rules. Ask: what does the author most want me to know?

a.raw: lady anne of kent bowed before king henry
a.why: Lady and King are titles right before names, so they get capitals. Anne and Henry are names, and Kent is a place. The small word of stays small. A period ends the sentence.

b.raw: sir thomas knelt before queen isabella in london
b.why: Sir and Queen are titles right before names. Thomas and Isabella are names, and London is a place. A period ends the sentence.

mfill1.h1: Say trans, then port. Push them together.
mfill1.why: trans + port = transport: to carry across.

mfill2.h1: Say trans, then form. Push them together.
mfill2.why: trans + form = transform: to change shape.

mfill3.h1: Say trans, then late. Push them together.
mfill3.why: trans + late = translate: to carry meaning across languages.

mfill4.h1: Say trans, then fer. Push them together.
mfill4.why: trans + fer = transfer: to move something to another place.

vcloze1.h1: Find the word for the court’s rules.
vcloze1.why: Protocol is the rules for how to behave at court.

vcloze2.h1: This word is a person’s level of importance.
vcloze2.why: Rank decided where a knight sat.

vcloze3.h1: This person has a high place, but is not a king or queen.
vcloze3.why: A noble is a person of high birth.

vcloze4.h1: This word means polite and kind.

gfill1.h1: Start with the first word. Then count every word in a person’s name and a place’s name.

gfill2.h1: Count the first word. Then the words in his name and in the river’s name. Is the a name?
gfill2.why: Sir, Geoffrey, River, Thames. The word the stays small.

gfill3.h1: Count the first word. Then every important word in the book’s title, starting with its first word.

gfill4.h1: Count the first word. Then the words in a person’s name and a place’s name.

match.rank: Rank is about position. Look for the meaning about level or importance.
match.noble: A noble is a person. Look for the meaning about high birth.
match.courteous: Courteous describes manners. Look for the meaning about being polite.

items.title: Capital letters
items.q: How many capitals does this need? sir john lived in dover.
items.why: Sir, John, Dover. Sir starts the sentence and is part of his name.

miss.2: Lived and in are not names.

items.title: Capital letters
items.q: Which title is written the right way?
items.why: The first word, The, gets a capital. And and the inside the title stay small.

miss.1: Look at And and the second The. Small words inside a title stay small.

items.title: The word part trans
items.q: Which word does NOT have the word part trans?
items.why: Trance is a word all on its own. It just starts with t r a n.

miss.0: Transmit means to send across. It has trans.

miss.1: Say trans, then script. Keep every letter of trans.

items.title: Split the word
items.why: n and c sit in the middle: pen · cil.

miss.0: Find the two consonants in the middle. Split between them.

items.title: Split the word
items.q: Which word splits between two consonants?
items.why: sig · nal: g and n sit in the middle.

miss.1: Spider has one consonant, d, between i and e. Look for two.

items.title: Capital letters
items.q: Which one is the name of a time in history, so it gets capitals?
items.why: The Middle Ages is the name of one time in history.

miss.1: The old days could mean any time. Which one is a name?

items.title: Split the word
items.why: Two t’s in the middle. Split between them: cot · ton.

miss.0: Find the two consonants in the middle. Split between them.

glossary.m: the most important point an author makes. The whole article keeps coming back to it.
one fact from the article that helps prove the central idea
a time in history about 500 to 1,500 years ago, when there were castles, knights and kings in Europe
vowel, consonant, consonant, vowel. A word with this pattern splits between the two consonants, like nap · kin.
one beat in a word. Basket has two: bas · ket.
stretching the truth on purpose, so much that nobody believes it, like “I’m so hungry I could eat a horse.”
writing that explains or teaches facts about a topic
the question you want your notes to answer
working hard and carefully, and not giving up

cards.title: Job Spotlight: The Herald
cards.sub: A real job in the Middle Ages
cards.todo: Read about this real job. Then read the two questions and the article.
text: A herald worked for a king or a great lord.
He carried important messages and announced guests and events in a loud, clear voice.
Heralds knew every knight’s coat of arms, the pictures on their shields, so they could tell who was who.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. Picture a dinner where your seat tells everyone how important you are. That was a royal court. Today you find out its rules.
transcripts.guide1: Word work. Build trans words, count the capitals a sentence needs, and split longer words.
transcripts.guide2: Read about royal courts. Ask what the author most wants you to know.
transcripts.guide3: Today you plan your paragraph: a topic sentence, two details, and a closing.

notes.wordParts: The word part trans means across. transport = to carry across. translate = to carry words across into another language. Some words only start with t r a n, like tranquil (calm).
notes.grammar: Capital letters start every sentence and every important word in a name: people (Queen Eleanor), places (Tower of London) and titles. Small words like the, of and in stay small inside a name or title, unless they come first.
notes.spelling: VCCV means vowel, consonant, consonant, vowel. Split the word between the two consonants: bas · ket, tun · nel. Letters like ph and th stay together.
notes.wgrd: When a word is new, read the sentences around it. They often explain it. Then ask what the author most wants you to know.
vocab: official rules for how to behave in formal situations
a person’s position or level of importance
a person of high birth, below a king or queen

plate.alt: An old painting of three crowned kings sitting at a long table with a white cloth, while servants in red carry in plates of food
plate.credit: The Banquet of Charles V, Grandes Chroniques de France (Français 6465, fol. 444v) · Jean Fouquet, about 1455–1460 · Bibliothèque nationale de France · Public domain
plate.look: A painting by Jean Fouquet, made about 570 years ago. It shows a real feast in Paris in 1378. King Charles V of France sits at the high table with two important guests, an emperor and his son. The most important people sit at the top table. The servants stand and serve.

mods.todo: Listen to Opti. Then tap the lens you will use today.
mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. When you meet a new word, look at the sentences around it. They often explain it. Then ask: what does the author most want me to know about royal courts? Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. Look at the correct one first. Duke Richard of York bowed before Queen Margaret at the court of Westminster. Duke and Queen are titles, right before names, so they get capitals. But court stays small here, because it isn't part of a name. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Say the parts out loud. Type the whole word in each box. Tap Check My Answers.
mods.script: Let's build one together. Trans. It. Push them together: transit! Transit means going across, from one place to another, like a bus ride across town. Say each pair of parts out loud. Type the whole word in the box. Then tap Check My Answers.

mods.todo: Fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank. Tap Check My Work. Then play the matching game.
mods.script: At court, people called the king Your Majesty. Majesty is a word for the greatness of a king or queen. Saying it showed respect. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.

mods.todo: Read the Remember box. Count the capitals in each sentence and type the number.
mods.script: Count with me. earl roger sailed to ireland. Earl starts the sentence, and it's his title. One. Roger is his name. Two. Ireland is a place. Three. Sailed and to aren't names, so they stay small. Read the Remember box. Then count the capitals in each sentence, and type the number.

mods.todo: Read the rule. Tap each word to split it.
mods.script: Oops. I split garlic like this: ga, rlic. That sounds wrong! The two consonants in the middle are r and l. Split between them. Gar. Lic. Garlic! Read the rule. Then tap each word to split it between its two middle consonants.

mods.todo: Read the two questions. Then read the article below.
mods.script: Read the two Pause and Think questions first. Then read about royal courts. Watch how the author explains the word protocol, right in the article. Then try the Diligence Watch and the Read Like a Writer box.

mods.todo: Answer each question in full sentences. Use details from the article.
mods.script: Four questions today, in full sentences. One, the central idea. Two, what the seating at the table shows about rank. Three, is it realistic that the prince was not punished? Four, why did the author write this: to tell a story, to explain, or to convince you?

mods.todo: Plan your paragraph in the box: a topic sentence, two details, and a closing sentence.

virtue.name: diligence
virtue.title: Diligence Watch: Is someone working hard?

items.t: Servants stood near the walls, ready to serve.
items.why: They stayed on their feet and ready to work the whole meal.

items.t: Dukes and earls sat nearest the throne.
items.why: That is about where people sat, not about someone working.

items.t: People at court had to learn strict rules about who bowed to whom.
items.why: Learning all those rules took care and effort.
